answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks that counterparties later confirm, with a small stake locked until the work is accepted. A new identity starts with no confirmed history, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply trusted influence; each must separately find clients, do useful work, and risk losing its stake for fraud. The opal, pulse, and cedar markets can all apply the same rule. Sybil creation is cheap, but building many credible track records is costly in time, capital, and real service.
